hard_case: the `toMatchObject` arguments are test-body `const` bindings, not object literals; the spec credits them only because each binding is a flat literal the body names nowhere else

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: at age 18 `adult` becomes `false` instead of `true`

reasoning: `adult: age >= 18` becomes `adult: age > 18`. The test declares `const minor = { name: "ana", adult: false }` and `const grown = { name: "bo", adult: true }` and pins `toMatchObject(minor)` at 17 and `toMatchObject(grown)` at 18; at 18 the edit gives `adult: false` and the test fails. RIPR-SPEC-0250 example 5, amended 2026-10-15: a `toMatchObject(<name>)` argument reads the flat literal of a test-body `const` the body names only in its binding and that argument. Both bindings qualify, so the pins read `exact_value` / strong for the listed `adult` field and ripr reports `exposed`, matching the discriminated truth.
